guide.title: MP4 to F4V: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

An MP4 file follows MPEG-4 Part 14, written ISO/IEC 14496-14, which appeared in 2003. It builds on the ISO Base Media File Format, whose nested boxes come from QuickTime. Most files hold H.264 video and AAC audio, though AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus can be inside as well. Video uses the endings .mp4 and .m4v, and every major browser plays it.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay plays MP4 files whose streams the installed FFmpeg build can decode, and mpv offers audio-track switching.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports MP4 when a suitable decoder is present.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play supported MP4 files directly.
- **Mobile:** VLC on Android and on iOS.

### MP4 and F4V compared

F4V, an Adobe format, borrows its layout from the MPEG-4 container. That makes it a wrapper rather than a codec, so the streams inside matter more than the ending. Flash Player support has ended and no current browser plays Flash, which leaves F4V for archives and older Flash projects.

FFmpeg, compiled to WebAssembly, deinterlaces the video, encodes it as H.264 and writes AAC audio at 96 kbps. Footage whose long edge exceeds 1920 px is downscaled, and a rate above 30 fps is brought down by dropping frames; smaller values stay. Each side is then made even, which costs an odd side one pixel. Files are processed one at a time, and the MP4 you chose is not modified.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to F4V

- **FFmpeg, re-encoding:** run `ffmpeg -i lesson.mp4 -c:v libx264 -c:a aac -f f4v lesson.f4v` to write H.264 video and AAC audio into an F4V.
- **FFmpeg, stream copy:** run `ffmpeg -i compatible.mp4 -c copy -f f4v compatible.f4v` to copy the streams without re-encoding. Use it when the MP4 already holds H.264 video and AAC audio.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **Sound or picture missing:** the file ending says nothing about which decoders a player has. Try another player, such as mpv.
- **A recording that stopped early:** MP4 gathers the index of its packets in one place, so a write cut short may leave an unplayable file.

guide.title: MP4 to M2TS: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

Phone clips, camera footage and downloaded web video usually arrive as MP4, which is MPEG-4 Part 14. It is standardized as ISO/IEC 14496-14 and dates from 2003. The file is a tree of boxes, the idea QuickTime calls atoms. Video takes .mp4 or .m4v, audio-only files often take .m4a, and the media types video/mp4 and audio/mp4 cover it.

### Programs that open MP4 files

To play the source MP4 before copying it:

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay uses FFmpeg's libraries and mpv switches between audio streams.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere reads an MP4 when a decoder is available for its contents.
- **Web:** Firefox plays MP4 and may lean on codecs supplied by the operating system for AAC and H.264, while Chrome handles the combinations it supports.
- **Mobile:** VLC on iOS and Android.

### MP4 and M2TS compared

M2TS packages video, audio and further streams for Blu-ray BDAV and AVCHD. It adapts the MPEG-2 transport stream and does not prescribe one video codec. Every source packet wraps a 188-byte transport packet and adds four bytes. Blu-ray permits MPEG-2, AVC and VC-1 pictures in it. Sony and Panasonic announced AVCHD in 2006.

FFmpeg runs in your browser and copies the streams from the MP4 without re-encoding. The picture therefore keeps its size and frame rate, and the 1920 px and 30 fps cap that other video pages apply is not in play. Each file downloads on its own, and the MP4 itself is not altered.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to M2TS

- **FFmpeg, stream copy:** run `ffmpeg -i concert.mp4 -c copy -mpegts_m2ts_mode 1 concert.m2ts`. The `-mpegts_m2ts_mode 1` option enables M2TS mode.
- **FFmpeg, re-encoding:** run `ffmpeg -i delivery.mp4 -c:v libx264 -c:a ac3 -mpegts_m2ts_mode 1 delivery.m2ts` to write new H.264 video and AC-3 audio instead of copying.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **A missing decoder:** a player can accept the MP4 and still lack the decoder for what it holds, which gives a blank picture or silence. Try another player.
- **An unfinished file:** MP4 keeps its packet index together, so a recording cut off while writing may produce a file no player can open.

guide.title: MP4 to RM: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

Most phones and cameras save video as MP4, defined by MPEG-4 Part 14, ISO/IEC 14496-14, published in 2003. Boxes nest inside boxes, a layout inherited from QuickTime through the ISO Base Media File Format. A typical MP4 holds H.264 pictures and AAC sound, although VP9 and Opus can also appear. Files end in .mp4 or .m4v, and audio-only MPEG-4 files frequently use .m4a.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay, which comes with FFmpeg, opens an MP4, and mpv can choose among audio tracks.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere takes in an MP4 when it has the decoder for the contents.
- **Web:** Chrome and Firefox play the MP4 combinations they support.
- **Mobile:** the VLC apps for Android and iOS.

### MP4 and RM compared

RM is RealMedia. RealNetworks described it as a streaming container in an Internet-Draft dated March 1998, covering playback from local storage or over a network. A RealMedia file begins with a .RMF header and continues in tagged chunks with four-character identifiers. Separate headers describe the whole file and each stream. The draft is work in progress, so its version-specific structures are history, not a guarantee.

The command here is plain: FFmpeg reads the MP4 and writes an .rm file, with no codec options of its own. The page first tries a server route and then converts in your browser with FFmpeg. You still get a separate download for each file, and your original is untouched.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to RM

- **FFmpeg with RealVideo 1.0 and AC-3:** run `ffmpeg -i exhibit.mp4 -c:v rv10 -b:v 800k -c:a ac3 exhibit.rm`. The `-b:v` option sets the video bitrate.
- **FFmpeg, silent:** run `ffmpeg -i display.mp4 -an -c:v rv20 -b:v 800k display.rm` to leave out all sound and use RealVideo 2.0.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **Silent or black playback:** a player needs a decoder for every stream in the file, and the ending does not promise one. Try another player, such as mpv.
- **A cut-off recording:** MP4 stores its packet index in one place, so an interrupted write may leave a file nothing can play.
- **Nothing for an audio editor:** an MP4 with no audio track gives an editor nothing to import.

guide.title: MPEG to WMV: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is an MPEG file?

MPEG video follows one of the Moving Picture Experts Group standards. MPEG-2, the generation behind DVD video, was designed for compressed television. Systems layers organize picture, sound and data as streams: an elementary stream is one coded component, and packetized elementary streams cut it into packets. The endings .mpeg and .mpg are both common, and the Library of Congress lists video/mpeg as the media type.

### Programs that open MPEG files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player opens MPEG elementary, program and transport streams, while ffplay decodes MPEG.
- **Mobile:** on phones, the Android version of VLC brings desktop decoding, and the iOS version plays local files with its own player.

### MPEG and WMV compared

ASF, the wrapper around a .wmv file, exists to keep synchronized media together for storage and for network delivery. The video can be coded as Windows Media Video 7, 8 or 9, but this page writes MS-MPEG4 v3 instead. The Library of Congress records video/x-ms-wmv as the usual media type.

FFmpeg re-encodes the video in your browser and leaves the codecs to its WMV defaults: MS-MPEG4 v3 at 200 kbit/s and WMA v2 audio. Interlaced frames are deinterlaced. Longer sides above 1920 px and rates above 30 fps are reduced by the converter, and an odd width or height then gives up a pixel. Both formats are lossy, so this is a second lossy pass. Files are handled one by one.

### Other ways to convert MPEG to WMV

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i seminar.mpeg -c:a wmav2 -b:v 1200k -c:v wmv2 seminar.wmv`. It names WMV2 video and WMA v2 audio, and `-b:v` fixes the video bitrate, unlike the page's defaults.

### Problems with MPEG files

- **Unclear structure:** an MPEG file may be a system stream or bare video, and identifying which helps choose the correct demuxer.
- **Picture but no sound:** the audio track needs its own decoder in the player, separate from the video one, and putting both in one file does not supply it.
- **Softer detail:** MPEG compression discards some of the original picture, and each further lossy pass discards more.

guide.title: NEF to PDF: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is a NEF file?

NEF, short for Nikon Electronic Format, is the raw photo file written by Nikon cameras. It preserves the sensor's capture together with camera and lens metadata, either uncompressed or losslessly compressed, at 12 or 14 bits depending on the camera. White balance, hue, tone and sharpening may be recorded as separate instructions rather than applied to the pixels, and Nikon's software can output a JPEG or TIFF while the raw file stays as shot.

### Programs that open NEF files

- **Windows and Mac:** NX Studio is Nikon's program for viewing and developing NEF photos.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick reads NEF, a read-only format in its formats list.
- **Linux:** XnView MP supports NEF and costs nothing for private or educational use.

### NEF and PDF compared

A PDF is a document format. It came from Adobe's Camelot project under John Warnock, begun in 1991 and named PDF by 1992, aiming for pages that show or print the same everywhere. ISO 32000-1 standardized PDF 1.7 in 2008. A page can mix text, vector art and bitmaps, and bitmaps are compressed losslessly with Flate or with JPEG. The media type is application/pdf.

In your browser, ImageMagick reads one image from the NEF. The PDF gets a single page cut to the picture, one point per pixel and no margin, with the picture stored inside as a lossless PNG. Several files are never merged, and your NEF is left alone.

### Other ways to convert NEF to PDF

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick selection.nef selection.pdf`. Its formats page marks NEF as readable and PDF as readable and writable, and PDF output requires Ghostscript.

### Problems with NEF files

- **It looks different after development:** white balance and other rendering settings are instructions that processing software applies, so the picture can change between programs.
- **The raw data is gone:** a JPEG export or a PDF is a rendered result and cannot stand in for the adjustable sensor data in the NEF. Keep the original.
- **Less tonal range:** tonal depth varies by camera, and an eight-bit export cannot hold the 12-bit or 14-bit depth of the raw file.

guide.title: ORF to JPEG: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is an ORF file?

ORF is the raw-picture extension of Olympus cameras, and of OM SYSTEM cameras since the brand changed. A file stores raw sensor readings in a TIFF-based layout with a JPEG preview embedded. Which cameras a program can read depends on its version; Adobe's table, for example, starts OM-1 ORF support at Camera Raw 14.2. Many photographers shoot ORF so they can edit before exporting JPEGs. OM Workspace, the maker's software, develops ORF files, adjusts white balance and exposure, and keeps a history of your processing so an edit can be undone back to the original settings.

### Programs that open ORF files

- **Windows and Mac:** OM Workspace comes from the camera maker and processes raw files. Adobe Camera Raw reads ORF too, with a minimum version that depends on the exact camera.
- **Linux:** ImageMagick reads ORF as a camera raw format, as long as the needed delegates are installed on your system.

### ORF and JPEG compared

The Joint Photographic Experts Group gave JPEG its name and began its work in 1986; ITU-T T.81 followed in 1992 and ISO/IEC 10918-1 in 1994. The method is lossy, works on 8x8 blocks and stores 8 bits per color channel. It has no layers and no alpha channel, though an optional progressive mode first draws a rough image and refines it as the file loads. Both .jpg and .jpeg name the format, its media type is image/jpeg, and every major browser displays it. Photos on web pages, in email attachments and on sharing sites are usually JPEG.

ImageMagick, working inside your browser, reads one image from the ORF and writes a JPEG. No quality setting is passed. With several files, each is converted in its turn and saved separately, and the ORF itself is untouched.

### Other ways to convert ORF to JPEG

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick portrait.orf portrait.jpeg`. In the formats list, ORF is read-only while JPEG can be read and written.

### Problems with ORF files

- **Camera not supported:** an older raw plug-in may lack your camera even though it opens other ORF files. Update the plug-in or the software.
- **A missing option:** in OM Workspace, not every processing option works with every raw image.
- **High Res Shot files:** OM Workspace needs 8 GB of memory or more to process them as raw.

guide.title: ORF to PNG: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is an ORF file?

Each ORF is a raw photograph from an Olympus or OM SYSTEM camera. It is TIFF-based, holds unprocessed sensor data and carries an embedded JPEG preview. Readers are matched to camera models and program versions, so a brand-new body can need an update before its files open. ORF mainly serves photographers who edit first and export afterwards. OM Workspace, from the manufacturer, develops them and logs your processing choices, which lets an edit step back to its starting settings.

### Programs that open ORF files

- **Windows and Mac:** OM Workspace is the maker's own raw software, and Adobe Camera Raw opens ORF once you look up the minimum version for your camera.
- **Linux:** ImageMagick treats ORF as a camera raw format; check that your install has the right delegates.

### ORF and PNG compared

PNG was created as a patent-free alternative to GIF and in October 1996 became the earliest format released as a W3C Recommendation; it was later published as RFC 2083 and ISO/IEC 15948:2004. DEFLATE compression discards nothing. A file starts with a signature and continues in chunks such as IHDR, IDAT and IEND. Samples run from 1 to 16 bits, and an optional alpha channel gives each pixel its own transparency. Browsers all display it, under the media type image/png. It suits screenshots, logos, pictures that need transparency and web graphics with crisp edges.

ImageMagick picks one image from the ORF and writes it out as PNG. The page passes no quality value, since lossless PNG has nothing to trade. Pick several ORFs if you like: each becomes its own PNG download, and the originals are never altered.

### Other ways to convert ORF to PNG

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick landscape.orf landscape.png`. Its formats page marks ORF as read-only and PNG as readable and writable; PNG output requires libpng.

### Problems with ORF files

- **Unsupported camera:** an older raw plug-in may skip your model yet read other ORF files. Update it.
- **Disabled options:** some processing options in OM Workspace are unavailable for some raw images.
- **Not enough memory:** processing High Res Shot raw files in OM Workspace takes 8 GB of memory at least.

guide.title: PBM to PNG: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is a PBM file?

PBM, short for Portable Bit Map, describes two-tone raster images, and Netpbm uses it as the glue between image-processing programs. The raw variant opens with P4 and packs its pixels bit by bit. The plain variant opens with P1 and spells pixels out as zeros and ones, with a one meaning black and a zero meaning white. Raw PBM permits consecutive images, while plain PBM contains one. The customary MIME label is image/x-portable-bitmap, which Netpbm notes is not registered with IANA.

### Programs that open PBM files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick reads PBM images, and XnView MP lists PBM among its readable formats. XnView MP is free for private and educational use.

### PBM and PNG compared

PNG started as a patent-free alternative to GIF and is standardized as ISO/IEC 15948:2004. Its compression loses nothing, and pictures can be indexed, grayscale or truecolor, with samples from 1 to 16 bits and transparency available through an alpha channel. A PBM carries only black and white, so a PNG made from it is a two-tone picture in a file that more programs can open. Every major browser shows PNG, and the media type is image/png.

Your browser runs ImageMagick here, and it takes one picture from the PBM. No quality setting is passed, since PNG has none to adjust. Add several PBMs and each is processed in turn and saved on its own; the originals stay as they were.

### Other ways to convert PBM to PNG

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick stencil.pbm stencil.png`. Its formats page marks both PBM and PNG as readable and writable.
- **Pillow:** in Python, after `from PIL import Image`, run `Image.open("mask.pbm").save("mask.png")`. Pillow reads plain and raw PBM and takes PNG from the file ending.

### Problems with PBM files

- **No shades:** color and gray shading cannot be represented directly in a two-tone image.
- **Large plain files:** a plain PBM spends a text digit on each pixel, so it takes more space than the raw form.
- **Partial readers:** some programs implement only a restricted part of the specification.
- **Several images in one file:** Netpbm recommends a minimal single-image layout for interoperability.

guide.title: PCX to JPG: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is a PCX file?

ZSoft created PCX as the native format of its PC Paintbrush program, which reached MS-DOS in 1984 and 1985. A picture is a raster with run-length encoding, palette-based or truecolor, and some variants add a second palette after the image data. PCX saw wide use on DOS and early Windows, and old clip art collections still turn up in it. A related DCX file bundles several PCX pictures, an arrangement common in fax software.

### Programs that open PCX files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick lists PCX for reading and writing, and Pillow, a Python imaging library, reads and writes PCX in the modes its documentation names.

### PCX and JPG compared

JPEG is named after the Joint Photographic Experts Group, active since 1986, and ITU-T T.81 followed in 1992. Baseline JPEG is lossy: it cuts the picture into 8x8 blocks, runs a discrete cosine transform, then Huffman-codes the result. Each channel gets 8 bits, there is no transparency, and the media type is image/jpeg. The endings .jpg and .jpeg are interchangeable, and web photos, email attachments and shared snapshots are mostly JPEG.

Run-length encoding in a PCX loses nothing, so the step to JPG adds a loss that was not there before. The conversion happens in your browser with ImageMagick, which decodes a single picture from the PCX. The page passes no quality setting. Each file is saved separately and your PCX stays as it is.

### Other ways to convert PCX to JPG

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick archive.pcx archive.jpg`. Its formats page marks both PCX and JPEG as readable and writable.
- **Pillow:** in Python, run `Image.open("clipart.pcx").convert("RGB").save("clipart.jpg")` after `from PIL import Image`. The `convert("RGB")` call turns a palette image into RGB before the JPEG is written.

### Problems with PCX files

- **A program rejects the file:** newer software sometimes drops PCX support while handling modern bitmaps. Convert it with one of the tools above.
- **Saving back to PCX:** Pillow's PCX writer accepts monochrome, grayscale, palette and RGB data, not arbitrary channel arrangements.
- **A DCX read as one PCX:** treating a DCX as a single PCX loses the document's multiple-image structure.

faqs.question: Can this page convert PES to JPG?
faqs.answer: No. The page passes the file to the browser's built-in image decoder, and a PES ends with the message 'Image decode failed.'

faqs.question: How do I get a picture of my embroidery design?
faqs.answer: Open the PES in software that draws stitches. Ink/Stitch imports a PES in Inkscape and can export a PNG, and ImageMagick on your computer can read a PES and write a JPG.

faqs.question: Will the JPG keep my stitches?
faqs.answer: No. A JPG is a flat picture with no stitch order, thread colors or machine instructions. Keep the PES for sewing.

faqs.question: Which programs open a PES file?
faqs.answer: Ink/Stitch on Windows, Mac and Linux, Brother's PE-DESIGN on Windows, and Brother's Artspira app on iOS and Android.

faqs.question: Can I rename the PES to JPG?
faqs.answer: No. Renaming changes only the ending, and the file would still contain embroidery data that no image viewer can read.

faqs.question: Does ImageMagick open PES files?
faqs.answer: ImageMagick lists PES as a format it can read, but not write. Run it on your own computer, as in the method above; it is a different engine from this page.

faqs.question: What do I do if my machine will not take the PES?
faqs.answer: The design may exceed the machine's USB-connected storage. Brother suggests a USB flash drive where supported.

faqs.question: Why would I want a JPG of an embroidery design?
faqs.answer: A JPG works as a preview you can share or print. It cannot be stitched, because it holds pixels rather than stitch data.

guide.title: PES to JPG: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is a PES file?

A PES file holds embroidery data for Brother's PE-DESIGN workflow, and Brother and Babylock machines use it. It stores stitch coordinates, a thread color palette and a design preview. PE-DESIGN 11 can show PES designs as thumbnails in Explorer in its full edition, and files saved by that version may be larger because they contain more design information. Ink/Stitch can both import and export PES, and Brother's Artspira app accepts PES files on iOS and Android. A PES describes stitches, not a grid of pixels.

### Programs that open PES files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Ink/Stitch is a free embroidery extension for Inkscape with PES import and export.
- **Windows:** PE-DESIGN 11 is Brother's application; its trial has restricted features.
- **Mobile:** Artspira accepts PES uploads on iOS and Android.

### PES and JPG compared

JPEG is a lossy picture format from the Joint Photographic Experts Group, standardized as ITU-T T.81 in 1992. It stores 8 bits per color channel, has no transparency and cannot hold layers. A JPG is a flat picture, so it cannot carry thread colors, stitch order or machine instructions, and it works only as a preview of the design. The media type is image/jpeg.

On this page the browser's own image decoder gets the file, and it stops on a PES with "Image decode failed." To get a JPG of a design, use software that draws the stitches, such as the programs below, and keep your PES for the sewing machine.

### Other ways to convert PES to JPG

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick sampler.pes sampler.jpg`. Its formats page lists PES for reading only, and JPEG for reading and writing.
- **Ink/Stitch:** open the PES with File > Open in Inkscape, then use File > Save a copy and pick PNG, one of the utility formats Ink/Stitch can write. Save a JPG from that PNG in any image editor.

### Problems with PES files

- **A color-change limit:** Ink/Stitch's troubleshooting page says a PES export cannot contain more than 255 color changes.
- **No thumbnails:** the PE-DESIGN 11 trial lacks the PES thumbnail integration of the full program.
